title: Mardi Gras and funeral parades in New Orleans
summary: He recalls carnivals, swimming at night and the slow funeral marches that turn lively with songs like Didn't He Ramble and The Saints.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You know, New Orleans is one of the most picturesque cities in America. You spent your childhood there. When you think back about New Orleans, do you ever want to, what comes through your mind?
Oh, well, the carnivals and the mardi gras were something to remember. Oh, yeah. We look forward to that. Everybody mass and the zoos, parade. Oh, boy. We used to go swimming at night, you know.

Yeah, the funerals. They take the body to the cemetery real slow. Everybody is serious, you know. And after the reverend, say ashes to ashes, dust to dust, you know what I mean? Yeah. They would kill the old brother Jones, his stomach arrest.
And then we go on back playing, didn't he ramble, oh, didn't he ramble.

And everybody jump in. Everybody's happy. And then when we get almost to the hall where they break up the parade, we put in them Saints Go Marching In. Oh, boy. And that's a traditional song. Yeah. When the Saints go. And everybody go to the saloon. And then...
